the modified coherence measure and speech-based STIs incorporating signal-specific band importance functions yielded the highest correlation with sentence recognition scores in fluctuating noise environments.

the modified coherence-based measure that only included vowel-consonant transitions and consonant information yielded a correlation of r=0.94 with sentence recognition scores, and that the proposed speech-based STI measure incorporating signal-specific band importance functions yielded the second highest correlation (r =0.93) with sentence recognition.

the design of new objective measures for predicting speech recognition in noisy conditions based primarily on the speech signal itself.
the development of objective measures for predicting speech reception in fluctuating noise.

the development and evaluation of new measures that can be applied for predicting speech intelligibilities in fluctuating maskers and that can be used for developing objective measures of speech intelligibility for speech communication systems.

a combination of signal- and segment-specific band-importance weighting, along with coherence-based measures that include only vowel/consonant transition and weak consonant features, would provide the best estimates for the intelligibility of speech in fluctuating noise environments.
the proposed coherence measures, which incorporate signal-specific band-importances, can provide an accurate estimate of speech intelligibility in fluctuating noise environments.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed coherence-based measures are able to predict intelligibility in fluctuating noisy conditions with higher accuracy than traditional AI- and STI-based metrics.
the new band-importance measures can be used to predict speech intelligibility in realistic fluctuating noisy conditions with greater accuracy than the current measures.

the new measures based on modified coherence and STI indices, incorporating the proposed signal- dependent band-importance functions, are promising candidates for the prediction of speech intelligibility in fluctuating noise environments.
